key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with ferroelectric materials could jointly supply local power and enable low-energy in-memory computing for edge AI, making distributed intelligence more practical.
engineering_relevance: The work points to a co-designed hardware stack—energy harvesting, storage, and computation—that can reduce communication energy and dependence on centralized data centers.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaics as local power sources for edge devices
Compare emerging materials against the energy needs of distributed intelligence
Argue that (anti)ferroelectrics can support both electrostatic energy storage and neuromorphic/in-memory computing
evidence_signal: This is a perspective paper that synthesizes requirements and materials progress rather than presenting new experimental datasets or benchmark evaluations.
watch_item: A key challenge is that reliable deployment still depends on closing gaps in indoor photovoltaic performance, storage integration, and low-power device engineering under real-world conditions.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
